newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad mulls div after rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad mulls div after rate rise.

text.p: Venezuela's Electricidad de Caracas, the bellwether stock on the Caracas Stock Exchange, is reviewing its dividend policy in the light of a recent rate increase, a top company official said Tuesday.
"We are still very conservative and still revising the numbers but we obviously have to do something soon," Freddy Cabrera, executive manager of sales, told Reuters.
Electricidad suspended nearly all of its regular quarterly cash and share dividends in 1996 due to delays in receiving approval for rate increases.

The possible change follows a rate increase authorized Friday of 5.16 percent for industrial and commercial users, and 30.2 percent for the residential users that account for over one third of Electricidad's billing.

"Overall the rises translate into a 10.4 percent increase in our rates," said Cabrera. While that falls short of a hoped-for 13 percent rise, "it does represent the first step in the slow elimination of cross-subsidies," he said.
